article: Aether (Physics): the luminiferous aether and its historical and modern meanings
scope: Corrected the Japanese source and completed full AI source-to-translation reviews for all 12 translated editions: English, German, Spanish, French, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese. Every record identifies exact source and translation hashes. Human/native-language confirmation is not claimed. Publication and live verification are pending.
findings: Qualified the status of aether in 19th-century physics and clarified that wave phenomena do not by themselves prove a mechanical medium.
Clarified that Maxwell’s equations do not themselves establish a mechanical aether or absolute rest frame.
Replaced the claim of literally zero fringe shift with the paper’s approximately 0.4-fringe expected displacement and a bounded null result.

Avoided dismissing Lorentz’s work as merely ad hoc and clarified that special relativity removes the need for a luminiferous mechanical medium without banning Einstein’s later distinct use of the word aether.

Revised the vacuum discussion to describe fields and their ground state without literalizing continuous particle-pair creation, and removed the false analogy between dark matter/dark energy and light-carrying aether.
Corrected the English and Arabic editions throughout the affected passages; other translations are still pending review.
Corrected the German edition throughout the affected historical and physics passages; other translations remain pending review.
Corrected the Spanish edition throughout the affected passages and reframed the experiment as a null result, not a failed measurement; other translations remain pending review.
Corrected the French edition throughout the affected passages, including a more precise account of the null result; other translations remain pending review.
Corrected the Hindi edition throughout the affected passages, including the distinction between the classical aether and quantum fields; other translations remain pending review.
Corrected the Indonesian edition throughout the affected passages and distinguished the null result from a failed measurement; other translations remain pending review.
Corrected the Korean edition throughout the affected passages and clarified that special relativity removes the need for a mechanical light medium; other translations remain pending review.
Corrected the Portuguese edition throughout the affected historical and physics passages; native Portuguese and regional usage confirmation remain outstanding.
Corrected the Russian edition throughout the affected passages and replaced the inaccurate absolute-zero fringe claim with a bounded null result.
Corrected the Simplified Chinese edition throughout the affected passages, including the distinction between quantum fields and a mechanical aether.
Corrected the Traditional Chinese edition throughout the affected passages and removed the misleading comparison between dark matter/energy and aether.

meaning.note: Compared all eight sections with the Japanese source and corrected the shared historical and physics overclaims. The English edition retains the source article structure and explains the limits of the 1887 result.

terminology.note: Checked luminiferous aether, preferred frame, interferometer/fringe displacement, null result, Lorentz transformation, quantum-field vacuum, dark matter, and dark energy.

mathematics.note: Checked the use of c and the statement of an expected shift of about 0.4 fringe against the cited 1887 paper. No derivation or other displayed equation is present.

code.note: Checked the sole Mermaid overview and updated its arrows so it presents stationary aether as a historical model, not a requirement of Maxwell’s equations. No executable software code is present.

links.note: There are no article hyperlinks in this edition. Factual corrections were checked against the primary 1887 Michelson–Morley paper, Maxwell’s 1865 paper, Einstein’s 1905 paper and 1920 address, and NASA explanations of dark matter and dark energy. External link reachability is not applicable.

limitations: Review performed by Codex (AI); no human or native English-language reviewer has confirmed style or terminology.
The account is a concise historical overview and does not survey every ether model or every later interferometer test.
Quantum-field vacuum language is introductory; it avoids treating virtual particles as literal particles continuously appearing and disappearing.
